panels.visual: A Cypriot merchant ship with purple dye barrels sinking in a storm, Zeno clinging to a plank
panels.caption: Zeno came from Cyprus as a merchant with a cargo of purple dye. His ship was wrecked.

panels.visual: Zeno in a bookshop in Athens reading a scroll, a bookseller pointing out of the door at a passing philosopher
panels.caption: In a bookshop in Athens he asked where he could find men like Socrates.

panels.visual: The Painted Porch (Stoa Poikile): a long colonnade covered with battle paintings, Zeno teaching a crowd
panels.caption: He taught in the Painted Porch. His followers were called Stoics, after the stoa.

panels.visual: The slave Epictetus with his leg twisted by his master, calm face, a stern master, a sweat drop; no gore
panels.caption: A Stoic called Epictetus, born a slave, said calmly: 'You will break it.' Then: 'Did I not tell you?'
